extracted.intended_audience: journalists and consumers who evaluate or produce health care news, advertising, marketing, and PR messages
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and operational standards used by HealthNewsReview.org to evaluate health care journalism, news releases, advertising and other messages that influence consumers, with emphasis on accuracy, balance, independence and promotion of shared decision-making. Includes site policies on conflicts of interest and reviewer conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: improve public dialogue by helping consumers critically analyze claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of HealthNewsReview.org is to improve the public dialogue about health care by helping consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions and by promoting the principles of shared decision-making reinforced by accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site evaluates journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers and provides criteria that consumers can use to evaluate these messages themselves. Improving the quality and flow of health care news and information to consumers is viewed as a step toward meaningful health care reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of materials evaluated
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org evaluates health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review focus explicitly includes both news stories and PR/news releases; the site produces criteria-driven reviews of those message types and offers a toolkit for journalists and consumers to apply the criteria themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard: accuracy, balance, and completeness about tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Health care coverage should provide accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is tied to promoting shared decision-making — reviewers look for reporting that explains what is known versus unknown and clarifies benefits, harms, costs, and tradeoffs rather than overselling interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: promote shared decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews and guidance should promote the principles of shared decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information evaluated should reinforce shared decision-making by helping consumers understand tradeoffs so they can make informed decisions with clinicians; the site emphasizes distinguishing what is known from what is not known in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from industry influence
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org does not accept advertising, nor do we accept funding from any entity whose support would represent a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No funder has editorial input; this independence is presented as necessary to ensure content has not been influenced directly or indirectly by commercial interests. The site treats lack of conflicted funding as a quality criterion for trustworthy review and commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer and expert conflict-of-interest policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All expert contributors pledge that they do not accept payments from drug or device companies or from any commercial entity whose support might represent a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the site quotes outside experts who are not team members, they will ask about any financial interests in the topic and disclose those interests in the article. The site also maintains a list of industry-independent experts for journalists to quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundaries: not a forum for definitive medical science or medical advice
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org is not equipped to host a definitive forum on medical science and does not give medical advice or act as an advocacy group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site sets explicit limits on its role and scope — it focuses on reviewing coverage and promotional messages rather than providing medical recommendations or advocacy, and it acknowledges resource limits in what it can review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational constraint: selection and maintenance of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The project cannot review every story or promotional message; reviews are selective and subject to resource constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site notes practical limitations (small editorial staff, budget) and communicates that archived, criteria-driven reviews may be removed when resources change; this transparency about capacity is part of the site's operational standards.
